# Supplementary Figure 2: fit score comparison of dd specific, dd bifactor, rdoc specific, and dd bifactor models
```{r}
# Function to extract and consolidate a specific fit measure from all subjects for a given model
extract_fit_measure <- function(results_list, model_name, measure_name) {
  # Initialize a vector to store the fit measures for all subjects
  fit_measures <- numeric(length(results_list))
  
  # Loop through the results list
  for (i in seq_along(results_list)) {
    # Try to extract the fit measure for the current subject
    # Dynamically access the correct model's output and then the specific fit measure using [[ for both levels
    fit_measure <- tryCatch({
      results_list[[i]][[model_name]]$fit.measures[[measure_name]]
    }, error = function(e) {
      NA  # In case of any error, assign NA
    })
    
    # Store the fit measure in the vector
    fit_measures[i] <- fit_measure
  }
  
  # Return the consolidated fit measures
  return(fit_measures)
}
```

# Create functions for violin plots for fit measures
```{r, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 5}
# Function to create a dataframe from the extracted measures
create_measure_df <- function(..., measure_names) {
  measures_list <- list(...)
  names(measures_list) <- measure_names
  
  # Finding the maximum length
  max_length <- max(sapply(measures_list, length))
  
  # Ensuring all vectors are of the same length
  measures_list <- lapply(measures_list, function(x) {
    if (length(x) < max_length) {
      length(x) <- max_length  # Extending the length of the vector and filling with NAs
    }
    x
  })
  
  # Convert the list to a data frame
  df <- bind_rows(lapply(names(measures_list), function(name) {
    measure <- measures_list[[name]]
    data.frame(Model = rep(name, length(measure)), RMSEA = measure, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }), .id = "ModelName")
  
  # Convert 'Model' to a factor and specify the order directly
  desired_order <- c("edd1", "eRDoC1", "edd2", "eRDoC2")
  df$Model <- factor(df$Model, levels = desired_order)
  
  return(df)
}

# Function to create violin plots with specified colors
create_violin_plot <- function(data, title = "Violin Plot", xlab = "Model", ylab = "Score") {
  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Model, y = RMSEA, fill = Model)) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, fill = "white", outlier.shape = 21, outlier.colour = "black", outlier.fill = "black", outlier.size = 1.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.background = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
    labs(title = title, x = xlab, y = ylab) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(
      "dd1" = hcl(240, 80, 40),
      "RDoC1" = hcl(10, 80, 40),
      "dd2" = hcl(240, 80, 40),
      "RDoC2" = hcl(10, 80, 40)
    ))

  if (tolower(ylab) %in% c("rmsea", "aic")) {
    p <- p + scale_y_reverse()
  }

  return(p)
}

# Build long df for a metric
build_metric_df4 <- function(dd1, dd01, rdoc01, rdoc1,
                             dd2, dd02, rdoc02, rdoc2,
                             metric_label) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(Cohort = "Cohort 1", Model = "DD",      value = as.numeric(dd1)),
    tibble::tibble(Cohort = "Cohort 1", Model = "DD-b",    value = as.numeric(dd01)),
    tibble::tibble(Cohort = "Cohort 1", Model = "RDoC",    value = as.numeric(rdoc01)),
    tibble::tibble(Cohort = "Cohort 1", Model = "RDoC-b",  value = as.numeric(rdoc1)),
    tibble::tibble(Cohort = "Cohort 2", Model = "DD",      value = as.numeric(dd2)),
    tibble::tibble(Cohort = "Cohort 2", Model = "DD-b",    value = as.numeric(dd02)),
    tibble::tibble(Cohort = "Cohort 2", Model = "RDoC",    value = as.numeric(rdoc02)),
    tibble::tibble(Cohort = "Cohort 2", Model = "RDoC-b",  value = as.numeric(rdoc2))
  ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(value)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Model  = factor(Model, levels = c("DD","DD-b","RDoC","RDoC-b")),
      Metric = metric_label
    )
}

# Plot a metric; reverse y for "lower is better" indices
plot_metric4 <- function(df, reverse = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Model, y = value, fill = Model)) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, fill = "white", outlier.size = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE) +
    facet_wrap(~ Cohort, nrow = 1) +
    labs(x = "Model", y = unique(df$Metric), title = unique(df$Metric)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(
      "DD"     = hcl(240, 50, 65),
      "DD-b"   = hcl(240, 80, 40),
      "RDoC"   = hcl( 10, 80, 40),
      "RDoC-b" = hcl( 10, 50, 65)
    )) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
          legend.position = "none")
  if (reverse) p <- p + scale_y_reverse()
  p
}
```

# Function for Repeated-measures ANOVA + Tukey, with labeled output
```{r, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 5}
# Build subject-long data for one cohort/metric
.make_long <- function(dd, dd_b, rdoc, rdoc_b, cohort, metric) {
  L <- max(length(dd), length(dd_b), length(rdoc), length(rdoc_b))
  pad <- function(x, L) { x <- as.numeric(x); length(x) <- L; x }
  wide <- data.frame(
    DD       = pad(dd,     L),
    `DD-b`   = pad(dd_b,   L),
    RDoC     = pad(rdoc,   L),
    `RDoC-b` = pad(rdoc_b, L),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  wide <- wide[complete.cases(wide), , drop = FALSE]
  wide$Subject <- factor(seq_len(nrow(wide)))
  long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(
    wide, c("DD","DD-b","RDoC","RDoC-b"),
    names_to = "Model", values_to = "value"
  )
  long$Model  <- factor(long$Model, levels = c("DD","DD-b","RDoC","RDoC-b"))
  long$Cohort <- cohort
  long$Metric <- metric
  long
}

# RM-ANOVA + Tukey pairwise
.run_tests <- function(df) {
  aov_obj <- afex::aov_ez(
    id = "Subject", dv = "value", data = df,
    within = "Model", type = 3,
    anova_table = list(correction = "GG", es = "ges")
  )
  emms  <- emmeans::emmeans(aov_obj, ~ Model)
  tukey <- emmeans::contrast(emms, method = "pairwise", adjust = "tukey")
  list(anova = aov_obj, tukey = tukey)
}

# Reporting helper
report_results <- function(metric, cohort, res) {
  cat("\n==============================\n",
      metric, " | ", cohort, "\n",
      "==============================\n", sep = "")
  cat("ANOVA (GG-corrected):\n")
  print(res$anova$anova_table)
  cat("\nPost-hoc (Tukey, pairwise):\n")
  print(res$tukey)
}
```

# Perform GG-corrected stats test Repeated-measures ANOVA + Tukey
```{r, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 5}
# RMSEA
df_rmsea_c1 <- .make_long(dd1_rmsea, dd01_rmsea, rdoc01_rmsea, rdoc1_rmsea, "Cohort 1", "RMSEA (robust)")
df_rmsea_c2 <- .make_long(dd2_rmsea, dd02_rmsea, rdoc02_rmsea, rdoc2_rmsea, "Cohort 2", "RMSEA (robust)")
res_rmsea_c1 <- .run_tests(df_rmsea_c1)
res_rmsea_c2 <- .run_tests(df_rmsea_c2)
report_results("RMSEA (robust)", "Cohort 1", res_rmsea_c1)
report_results("RMSEA (robust)", "Cohort 2", res_rmsea_c2)
```

# Check whether GG correction is necessary (per metric/cohort)
```{r}
check_sphericity <- function(df, alpha = 0.05) {
  # expects columns: Subject (factor), Model (factor), value (numeric)
  df <- as.data.frame(df)
  df$Subject <- factor(df$Subject); df$Model <- factor(df$Model)

  ez_out <- ez::ezANOVA(
    data = df, dv = value, wid = Subject, within = .(Model),
    type = 3, detailed = TRUE, return_aov = TRUE
  )

  mauchly <- ez_out$Mauchly
  sphcorr <- ez_out$`Sphericity Corrections`

  p_mauchly <- if (nrow(mauchly)) as.numeric(mauchly$p[1]) else NA_real_
  gg_eps    <- if (nrow(sphcorr)) as.numeric(sphcorr$GGe[1]) else NA_real_
  hf_eps    <- if (nrow(sphcorr)) as.numeric(sphcorr$HFe[1]) else NA_real_

  # Rule: if Mauchly p<alpha, sphericity violated → recommend HF if hf_eps>0.75, else GG; otherwise none
  recommend <- if (!is.na(p_mauchly) && p_mauchly < alpha) {
    if (!is.na(hf_eps) && hf_eps > 0.75) "HF" else "GG"
  } else {
    "none"
  }

  list(mauchly = mauchly, epsilons = sphcorr,
       mauchly_p = p_mauchly, gg_epsilon = gg_eps, hf_epsilon = hf_eps,
       recommend = recommend)
}

report_sphericity <- function(metric, cohort, diag) {
  cat("\n---", metric, "|", cohort, "---\n", sep = " ")
  cat("Mauchly p:", format(diag$mauchly_p, digits = 3, scientific = TRUE), "\n")
  cat("GG ε:", round(diag$gg_epsilon, 3), " HF ε:", round(diag$hf_epsilon, 3), "\n")
  cat("Recommendation:", diag$recommend, "\n")
  cat("\nMauchly table:\n"); print(diag$mauchly, row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nSphericity corrections:\n"); print(diag$epsilons, row.names = FALSE)
}

# Examples using your long data frames:
rmsea_c1_diag <- check_sphericity(df_rmsea_c1); report_sphericity("RMSEA (robust)", "Cohort 1", rmsea_c1_diag)
rmsea_c2_diag <- check_sphericity(df_rmsea_c2); report_sphericity("RMSEA (robust)", "Cohort 2", rmsea_c2_diag)
cfi_c1_diag   <- check_sphericity(df_cfi_c1);   report_sphericity("CFI (robust)",   "Cohort 1", cfi_c1_diag)
cfi_c2_diag   <- check_sphericity(df_cfi_c2);   report_sphericity("CFI (robust)",   "Cohort 2", cfi_c2_diag)
tli_c1_diag   <- check_sphericity(df_tli_c1);   report_sphericity("TLI (robust)",   "Cohort 1", tli_c1_diag)
tli_c2_diag   <- check_sphericity(df_tli_c2);   report_sphericity("TLI (robust)",   "Cohort 2", tli_c2_diag)
```
